claims.text: The baseline Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy has a single-phase BCC structure.
The baseline Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy has high density.
The baseline Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy has insufficient room-temperature ductility and exhibits brittle fracture.
Minor Al addition followed by solutionizing and aging will induce a reticulated B2 phase in Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr.
The induced B2 phase will be ordered and Al-rich.
The B2 phase will form a continuous, percolating reticulated network at grain boundaries and within the BCC matrix.
A reticulated B2 network will act as a physical barrier that pins, deflects, or branches propagating cracks.
Crack deflection or branching by the B2 network will increase compressive fracture strain.
The expected ductility improvement depends on phase-network topology rather than simple solid-solution hardening.
A continuous ordered B2 matrix can produce high strength but brittle room-temperature compression behavior.
The modified alloy will have a compressive fracture strain more than 10% higher than the baseline alloy.
The modified alloy's compressive strength will be comparable to or slightly lower than that of a solid-solution-strengthened variant.
The modified alloy's compressive strength will remain higher than that of the baseline brittle state.
Al addition will increase the alloy density.
Because Al is lighter than Hf, Mo, and Ta, Al addition may decrease the density or leave it approximately unchanged.
Too little Al will fail to form a reticulated B2 network.
Too much Al will produce a continuous B2 matrix rather than a reticulated network.
A continuous B2 matrix will lead to low room-temperature compressive ductility.
Room-temperature compression testing will be performed at a strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1.
Improved ductility in the absence of detectable B2 would falsify the proposed B2-network mechanism.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis initially specifies increased density as the Al-addition trade-off, whereas the correction and uncertainty fields state that light Al should decrease density or leave it similar.
